implementation.archive_stream: CapabilityStream adapts client-scoped AssetReader into original ArchiveSource (Read+Seek); no ambient path exposed
implementation.main_clock: caller-provided elapsed milliseconds; original run_frame scheduler retained
implementation.input: FIFO native down/up/move/button/wheel descriptors; native modeless capture preserved
implementation.host_requests: real VM continuations, explicit completion only, request completion also capability-scoped
implementation.display: crysirror_frame::capture plan; shared engine composes it, no original whole-frame compositor call
implementation.audio: original commands preserved for shared engine routing; no AudioSystem
implementation.bootstrap: same authorized ResourceManager, other roots rejected

checks: Sparse 3 GiB asset stream seeks/reads requested bytes without allocating the full asset
Separate resource capabilities and private save trees
Persistence failure does not replace/delete previous save
Native install UserData aliases write only client Save mount and never import original resource saves
Escaping, resource writes and ambiguous filenames rejected
Unreadable initial save fails visibly instead of disappearing

limits: Native MoveFile requires atomic rename support absent from ClientStorage; returns an explicit unsupported backend error without touching the source.

Empty user directories exist within the current session and are not persisted as independent directory records. Existing unclassifiable unreadable/empty entries fail visibly instead of being mistaken for missing saves.
Embedding callers must retain an exclusive save writer lease; crysirror-bgi adapter does so before creating HostRuntime.
Original VM scheduler tick is bounded by its cooperative watchdog and VM memory/count budget; exact Cry instruction_budget accounting is not implemented.
Original VM contains trusted upstream unsafe code; compatibility adapter itself is safe and device-free.
Native CPU bitmap syscalls remain original compatibility implementations; this audit does not claim complete service extraction or all BGI operations.
